A table's column can now show, keep its room or go, as the data says. Three layout faults are fixed: a bound that
kept the wrong edge, a bound that held only the frame in a flow, and a fitted column that measured no rich text. The
mail no longer writes a cell that was hidden. The designer now previews tables, picture grids and columns where the
engine puts them.

**Documents change where they asked for something the engine did not do.** These are items with a `MinWidth`,
`MaxWidth`, `MinHeight` or `MaxHeight` bound, fitted columns of rich text, and cells hidden by a condition in a mail.
Every sample in the repository came out to the byte as before. Three properties are added to `TableColumn`, hence 0.13
rather than 0.12.1.

## New: a column shows, keeps its room or goes

`TableColumn` carries the three properties an item already has, read the same way. An empty value is absent, blank,
zero or false.

```json
"Columns": [
  { "Width": 15 },
  { },
  { "Width": 20, "ShowWhen": "Discount" },
  { "Width": 25 }
]
```

- **`Gone` is as if the column had never been declared.** Its cells go in every row, the header included. Its width
  goes to the columns that state none. A table whose every column states a width ends sooner, and nothing is stretched
  to fill it.
- **`Invisible` keeps its width and its share of each row's height, and draws nothing.** Its cells are neither tagged
  nor written in a mail.
- **`ShowWhen` and `HideWhen` are read where the table stands, never in a line of its list**, as its header is. A
  column is the same in every row, so a discount column shows for the invoices that have a discount. In a list of
  invoices, each table asks its own invoice.
- **A cell keeps its own visibility,** and the more hidden of the cell and its column wins.
- The message standing in for an empty list spans the columns that show. The grid strokes nothing for a column that is
  gone.
- `frisket check --fields` and `TemplateFields.Check` read a column's paths against the host's catalogue, at
  `/Columns/n/ShowWhen`.

The designer offers the three on each column. The content editor has no control for them and keeps them on the column,
whichever columns its rails add or take away. The schema describes them.

## Fixed: a bound kept the right edge and the foot

An item that states no position and is narrowed by a bound kept its right edge and its foot. A paragraph held to 50 mm
sat against the right margin, a picture in a grid against the right of its cell, and a group at coordinates in the
bottom corner. The edge that stays is now the one the author anchored: the right only when the item is held by its
right and not its left, and the foot likewise.

## Fixed: in a flow, a bound held only the frame

A bound was applied once everything had been measured against the column. As a result:
- a paragraph held to 50 mm was broken across the whole column and drawn 160 mm past its own frame;
- a picture kept the height of the full width, under a frame a quarter as wide;
- a stacked group was not held at all.

At coordinates it was right. The flow now does what that path does: it bounds the item, aligns what is left, then
breaks the text. A bounded item that asks for an alignment is placed by it.

## Fixed: a fitted column measured no rich text

A fitted column of rich text closed to its padding and broke every word onto a line of its own. That is the only text
the content editor writes. It is now as wide as its widest line, each run in its own font. A column that states a width
is no longer narrowed when the fitted columns beside it overrun, even if it also says `Fit`.

## Fixed: the mail wrote a cell that was hidden

A cell hidden by its own `ShowWhen` or `HideWhen` was left out of the page and written in the mail. It kept its token as
typed, since the binder fills nothing that is not going to appear: `{Name}` in a message where the page showed nothing.
It is now an empty cell, so the row stays under its headers.

## The designer's preview, held to the engine

Three files the test suite writes and the designer's harness lays out again cover tables, grids of pictures and flows
in columns. What they found in the preview, all older than this release:

- **fitted columns were drawn as shared ones,** and the panel had no control for them. It now has a checkbox and two
  bounds;
- **a picture in a grid took the height of its proportions rather than its row's,** and was drawn over the row below.
  Its margin also counted twice;
- **whatever followed a group in columns was drawn a column's worth too low.**

## Worth checking

- **An item with a bound and no position now keeps its left edge and its top.** Before, it kept its right and its foot.
  A template that relied on that position moves.
- **A bounded item in a flow changes size.** A paragraph wraps at its bound and grows taller; a picture is as tall as
  its proportions at its bound; a group is narrowed with what it holds.
- **A fitted column of rich text is as wide as its text** rather than as its padding.
- **A mail holding a cell hidden by a condition has an empty cell there** instead of the cell's text or token.
